$comment: Which architecture doc, skill or rule covers which code. Read by
scripts/check-docs.mjs, which reports when an area changed and the file
Prefixes, matched against repo-relative paths from `git diff --name-only`.
A file may map to more than one entry; every match is reported.
Keep this honest rather than complete: a mapping that fires on changes the
doc does not actually describe trains you to ignore the warning, which is
the only failure mode that matters for an advisory check. Areas no doc
describes — frontend/app/(main)/clubs and events, the club/event domain
model — are deliberately absent until someone writes the doc.
`rules` holds .claude/rules/*.md, the path-scoped files a session loads when
it reads matching code. Same signal: code changed, rule did not.
A rule's own `paths:` frontmatter is deliberately broader than its entry
here. Frontmatter decides when the rule is LOADED — backend-java.md wants to
load on every backend file. This map decides when you are NAGGED to re-read
it, so it lists only the paths whose change could make a bullet untrue.
Mapping the broad set here would fire on every backend commit and train you

api-and-caching.md.covers: The apiFetch boundary, the caching model, DTO mapping, error-status mapping, and the DTO contract both sides assert against

ci-cd-pipeline.md.covers: GitHub Actions, tiering, the ci-success gate, local CI parity, and the dependency pins the Trivy gate depends on

club-administration.md.covers: Club-scoped authority, the assignment table, invitations, and the /manage dashboard

authentication.md.covers: Email + password and Google sign-in, token handling, password reset and verification mail

user-roles.md.covers: RBAC: two platform roles, two club roles, JWT claims, endpoint authorisation

user-profiles.md.covers: Profile content and email preferences: the user_profiles / user_interests / user_notification_preferences tables, the full-replace PUT, the slug-keyed interest catalogue (now the taxonomy package), and the shared profile load the editor depends on

llm-api-key-management.md.covers: How the OpenAI key flows without being logged or baked into an image

database-lifecycle.reason: Migrations, seeding, the dev profile and the admin bootstrap are governed by a skill, not a doc. Read it before changing these.

s3-media.reason: Media on S3: the private-bucket presigned model, object keys and credential handling. The skill also records where the shipped code departs from it.

backend-clubs.md.reason: The assigned-id merge trap, the taxonomy contract and the seeder that calls create()

backend-java.md.reason: Layering, entity-collection exposure, log scrubbing. Mapped to the files its bullets cite, not to every backend file it loads on

db-migrations.md.reason: Numbering, immutability once pushed, and what may not go in a migration

contracts.md.reason: The one field list both suites assert against, and what a rename has to touch

frontend.md.reason: The apiFetch boundary, the build-time traps and the CSP. Mapped to the files its bullets cite

ci-and-build.md.reason: What gates what, the exhausted Tomcat lever, and the local/CI parity script

aws-handling.md.reason: The account it names, the deployed shape it describes, the S3 baseline a new bucket has to match, and the hook that enforces all of it
